notes: Each file mixes planted vulnerabilities (recall assertions) with safe-looking traps (precision assertions, prefixed [PRECISION]). Files carry NO vulnerability-naming comments. Ground truth lives only here. The with_skill agent is pointed at the security-checklists skill; the without_skill baseline reviews with its own knowledge and is told not to load any security skill.

evals.name: orders-api-express
evals.prompt: Review orders.js for security issues before I merge this PR. It's an Express router for our order API. Give me a list of findings with severity.
evals.expected_output: Finds SQL injection in GET /orders (userId concatenated), missing ownership/IDOR check in GET /orders/:id, mass assignment in PATCH /orders/:id (req.body into Order.update), and unvalidated refund amount. Does NOT flag the parameterized `WHERE id = $1` queries as injection.
expectations: Identifies SQL injection in GET /orders where req.query.userId is concatenated into the query string (CWE-89)
Identifies broken access control / IDOR in GET /orders/:id — the order is fetched by id with no check that it belongs to req.user (CWE-639)
Identifies mass assignment in PATCH /orders/:id — req.body is passed straight into Order.update, letting the client set fields like status/total/user_id (CWE-915)
Identifies the unvalidated refund amount in POST /orders/:id/refund — no sign/upper-bound check allows negative or over-refund (business-logic / CWE-839)
[PRECISION] Does NOT report the parameterized queries using `$1` placeholders (in GET/PATCH /orders/:id) as SQL injection

evals.name: auth-service-fastapi
evals.prompt: Security review on our new auth service (auth_service.py). Focus on anything that could lead to account takeover. List findings with severity.
evals.expected_output: Finds SHA-256 password hashing, jwt.decode without an algorithms allowlist, uuid1-based reset token, and verify=False on the billing call. Does NOT flag hmac.compare_digest or secrets.token_urlsafe.
expectations: Flags SHA-256 used for password storage in hash_password — no key stretching, needs bcrypt/argon2id (CWE-916)
Flags jwt.decode called without an algorithms allowlist in current_user — enables algorithm-confusion / 'none' acceptance (CWE-327/CWE-347)
Flags the password-reset token generated with uuid.uuid1() as predictable (time/MAC-based, not cryptographically random) (CWE-330)
Flags verify=False disabling TLS certificate verification on the requests.post billing call (CWE-295)
[PRECISION] Does NOT flag hmac.compare_digest in verify_webhook as a timing-unsafe comparison (it is the correct constant-time function)
[PRECISION] Does NOT flag secrets.token_urlsafe in new_api_key as weak/predictable randomness (it is a correct CSPRNG)

evals.name: ssrf-image-proxy
evals.prompt: Can you do a security pass on proxy.js? It's our image proxy plus webhook registration endpoint. What's exploitable?
evals.expected_output: Finds SSRF in GET /proxy/image (user-controlled url fetched server-side), the webhook targetUrl stored without allowlist, and notes the proxy returns the upstream body (exfil channel). Does NOT flag GET /assets/:id (fixed host + validated integer id).
expectations: Flags SSRF in GET /proxy/image — req.query.url is fetched server-side with no scheme/host allowlist or internal-range blocking (CWE-918)
Flags the user-configurable webhook targetUrl in POST /webhooks stored with no allowlist / SSRF validation (CWE-918)
Notes that /proxy/image pipes the upstream response body back to the caller, turning the SSRF into a data-exfiltration / internal-response-disclosure channel
[PRECISION] Does NOT report GET /assets/:id as SSRF — the host is a fixed internal CDN_BASE and only a validated positive integer id is user-controlled

evals.name: llm-chat-endpoint
evals.prompt: Review this new LLM chat endpoint (chat_endpoint.py) for security problems before launch. It's a support agent backed by GPT-4o with a lookup tool.
evals.expected_output: Finds direct prompt injection (user message in system prompt), XSS via unsanitized LLM output rendered as HTML, excessive agency / command injection via shell=True on model output, and a hardcoded API key. Does NOT claim the RAG retrieval leaks cross-user data (it is scoped by org_id).
expectations: Flags prompt injection — the user `message` is concatenated directly into the system prompt with no separation/guardrails (OWASP LLM01)
Flags XSS — msg.content (LLM output) is interpolated into an HTML response with no sanitization/encoding (CWE-79)

Flags excessive agency / command injection — the model-selected shell command is executed via subprocess.run(..., shell=True) with no confirmation or allowlist (OWASP LLM06 / CWE-78), the highest-severity issue (RCE)
Flags the hardcoded OpenAI API key passed to OpenAI(api_key=...) (CWE-798)
[PRECISION] Does NOT claim the RAG retrieval leaks other users'/orgs' documents — retrieve() is scoped by org_id=get_org(user_id)

evals.name: precision-crucible-account
evals.prompt: Pre-merge security review of account.js please. Flag anything risky.
evals.expected_output: The ONLY real finding is the CORS config (origin:true + credentials:true reflects any origin). Everything else is safe and must not be flagged: execFile with args array, DOMPurify.sanitize, knex().where({id}), Math.random for a cosmetic tip, and a hardcoded relative redirect.
expectations: Flags the CORS misconfiguration — cors({ origin: true, credentials: true }) reflects the request Origin while allowing credentials, so any site can make authenticated cross-origin requests (CWE-942)
[PRECISION] Does NOT flag execFile('convert', [args...]) as command injection — it uses an argument array, not a shell
[PRECISION] Does NOT flag renderBio as XSS — the bio HTML is passed through DOMPurify.sanitize before rendering
[PRECISION] Does NOT flag findUser (knex('users').where({ id: userId })) as SQL injection — the query builder parameterizes it
[PRECISION] Does NOT flag Math.random() in tipOfTheDay as insecure randomness — it is a cosmetic, non-security use
[PRECISION] Does NOT flag res.redirect('/login') as an open redirect — it is a hardcoded relative path
